overview.description: Lungau Königrufen is a regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Lungau region of Salzburg. It is known for being a faster, sharper game with fewer, more decisive contracts and a streamlined counting process.

history.origins: Lungau Königrufen is a streamlined regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Salzburger Lungau in central Austria. It developed from the traditional Tarock game with a reduced set of contracts (Sechserdreier, Rufer mit Spatz, Rufer mit Uhu, Dreier) and simplified card counting, producing a sharper, faster game than forms played elsewhere in Austria. Regular tournaments are held in the region; the variant is maintained and documented as a distinct local tradition.
timeline: 20th century: played in Salzburger Lungau; regional tournaments documented.
history.cultural: Strong local following in Salzburg province.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards; take a majority of card points (36 or more out of 71); score game points from the contract and bonuses; losers pay winners per game point.
rules.gameplay: Bidding. Contracts include Rufer, Solo, Sechserdreier. Calling a King. Talon usage depends on bid. Play follows standard Tarock rules (follow suit/trump).

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. Follow suit if possible; if unable to follow, must play a trump (Tarock) if held. Trick is won by highest trump in it, or if no trumps by highest card of led suit. Winner leads next trick.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit when possible; must trump when cannot follow and have a Tarock; cannot win trick if void in led suit and have no trumps.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Decline to bid or overcall (say Erster when first player, or pass when not wishing to bid).
pass.constraints: When not wishing to bid or overcall. If all four players pass, a Fahren (Trischaken) is played.

bid.description: Place a bid for a contract (Sechserdreier, Rufer mit Spatz, Rufer mit Uhu, or Dreier) or pass by saying Erster. Contracts are in ascending order; Sechserdreier can only be bid by the first player and ends the auction.
bid.constraints: First player may bid any contract or pass; others may pass or overcall in ascending order (Rufer mit Spatz, Rufer mit Uhu, Dreier). Sechserdreier only by first player and ends auction; Dreier ends auction.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: 22 Tarocks (Sküs highest, then XXI down to I).
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must play higher trump when trumping if possible.

engine.handRankingSystem: Card-point scoring: Sküs, XXI, I, Kings 5 pts; Queens 4; Knights 3; Jacks 2; total 71. Majority 36+ wins.
engine.deckDescription: A 54-card Industrie und Glück tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Skus and 32 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace, 2, 3, 4.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits are divided into black suits (Spades and Clubs) and red suits (Hearts and Diamonds), each with its own reduced pip sequence.
engine.rankDescription: Courts are King, Queen, Cavalier, and Jack. Black suits continue with 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits continue with Ace, 2, 3, 4. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Skus.
engine.dealPattern: 12 cards each in two batches of 6, counterclockwise from player to dealer's right; 6 cards to talon in two face-down packets of 3.

scoring.description: Card points (71 total); 36+ wins the game. Contract and bonuses in game points; losers pay winners per game point (e.g. 10 cents per point).
scoring.winCondition: The team with a majority of card points (36 or more out of 71) wins the game. Bonuses (Trull, Four Kings, Pagat Ultimo, Uhu, King Ultimo, etc.) add or subtract game points. Net score determines payment from losers to winners.
